title: A Seed Grows
author: Antoinette Portis
rationale: The botanical back matter (germination chemistry, photosynthesis, pollination ecology) and fold-out sunflower scale give 7-9 substantive plant science beyond the picture-book surface; each band engages a different depth layer of the same content.

title: Alexander and the Terrible Horrible No Good Very Bad Day
author: Judith Viorst
rationale: A fluent 7-9 reader decodes the single-thread emotional narrative in under 5 minutes; the Australian refrain is the only geographic hook and is too thin to constitute a second layer, leaving no substantive content the band hasn't already fully processed.

title: Anything
author: Rebecca Stead
rationale: The mathematical concept of infinity and the philosophical landscape of possibility carry genuine depth for all three bands; the 'how many anythings' spread functions as a visual puzzle 7-9 can engage mathematically while 3-4 experience it as wonder.

title: At the Window
author: Hope Lim
rationale: The implied-loss narrative and apartment-observation premise are calibrated for the 3-6 emotional range; at 7-9 the friendship-loss-reorientation sequence is processed quickly without a conceptual second layer that justifies the band.

title: Bartleby
author: Matt Phelan
rationale: Identity formation and resistance to social conformity are authentic 7-9 concerns as peer dynamics intensify; a 7-9 reading about a polar bear refusing to change his essential nature brings real social experience to the text that makes the concept genuinely substantive at this band.

title: Brave Irene
author: William Steig
rationale: Steig's elevated vocabulary and the genuine weather science (blizzard physics, wind chill, landmark navigation) give 7-9 substantive content beyond the determination narrative; the problem-solving logic when the dress flies away models resourceful reasoning the band can engage critically.

title: Chooch Helped
author: Andrea L. Rogers
rationale: The sibling-exhaustion premise is emotionally resonant but concept-thin for 7-9; a fluent reader decodes the entire emotional arc in a single sitting without encountering a second layer that requires the cognitive capacity of this band.

title: Chrysanthemum
author: Kevin Henkes
rationale: Though the linguistics content (names, etymology, weight of words) gestures toward 7-9 territory, the K-1 mouse-school format and concept depth read as 'for little kids' to a fluent 7-year-old; the name-teasing arc is fully decoded in under 5 minutes with no expanding layer.

title: Click Clack Moo: Cows That Type
author: Doreen Cronin
rationale: The civics content (collective bargaining, formal written demands, third-party mediation via Duck) and literacy-as-power theme carry genuine substance for all three bands; each band engages a different layer — 3-4 the comedy, 5-6 the writing mechanics, 7-9 the labor-rights structure.

title: Diary of a Spider
author: Doreen Cronin
rationale: The arachnid biology (webs, molting, silk production) is presented at picture-book density insufficient for 7-9 primary content; the diary format and concept weight are calibrated for 5-6 emerging readers, leaving no second layer for a fluent 7-9 reader.

title: Diary of a Worm
author: Doreen Cronin
rationale: The soil ecology content (decomposition, earthworm biology) is authentic but presented at early-reader picture-book density; by 7-9 the diary format is familiar and the science is too thinly layered to engage a fluent reader as primary content.

title: Doctor De Soto
author: William Steig
rationale: The ethical puzzle (professional duty vs. self-protection, trust violation and premeditated response) engages 7-9 moral reasoning; Steig's elevated vocabulary and the logical elegance of the glue solution reward a fluent reader's analytical attention.

title: Don't Eat the Birthday Boy!
author: Donna Barba Higuera
rationale: The impulse-vs.-relationship concept is thinly developed for 7-9; the monster-birthday-party comedy premise delivers the concept at picture-book density without a second layer that justifies the Artisan band.

title: Don't Trust Fish
author: Neil Sharpson
rationale: The epistemology content (unreliable narration, the difference between assertion and evidence) has genuine educational substance for 7-9 developing critical thinking; 3-4 engage the absurdist fish comedy while 7-9 engage the logic-of-truth-claims layer that underpins it.

title: Drum Dream Girl
author: Margarita Engle
rationale: The layered content (Cuban gender history, Afro-Cuban musical tradition, physics of percussion, Caribbean geography, verse poetry structure) gives 7-9 simultaneous academic hooks across history, music, and geography; each band extracts a different primary layer from the same text.

title: Enemy Pie
author: Derek Munson
rationale: The friendship-mechanics content (proximity and shared play dissolving hostility) is well within a 7-9's existing social understanding; the picture-book format delivers the concept without a second layer, and the father's method reads as charming rather than analytically engaging at this band.

title: Extra Yarn
author: Mac Barnett
rationale: Barnett's economic concept of abundance (an inexhaustible resource reveals character and transforms community) and the archduke's greed as a lesson in scarcity thinking give 7-9 genuine philosophical content; Klassen's layered visual storytelling rewards careful reading at this band.

title: Fireworks
author: Matthew Burgess
rationale: The light physics and urban geography content are present but delivered at visual picture-book density without the concept depth to sustain 7-9 engagement; the Caldecott-winning illustration experience is the primary value, which doesn't substitute for textual or conceptual weight at this band.

title: Fish and Wave
author: Sergio Ruzzier
rationale: Early-reader chapter format requires sustained reading comprehension that pre-literate 3-4 cannot follow; the abstract philosophical question of friendship with something always moving also exceeds Wonderer's concrete-operational ceiling.

title: Fox Has a Problem
author: Corey R. Tabor
rationale: Early-reader chapter format and the abstract logic of problem-definition (each animal solves the wrong problem) exceed Wonderer's pre-literacy requirement and concrete-operational thinking; the escalating mismatched-solutions structure requires sustained narrative comprehension beyond 3-4 attention span.

title: Fox Versus Fox
author: Corey R. Tabor
rationale: Early-reader format and the abstract identity/authenticity concept (which of two identical characters is 'real'?) both exceed Wonderer's concrete-operational and pre-literacy requirements; the comparison structure presupposes reading ability.

title: Frederick
author: Leo Lionni
rationale: The philosophical question 'what counts as useful labor in a community?' deepens for 7-9 who can engage the economics and ecology of invisible creative work; each reading yields a different layer — 3-4 the mice and seasons, 7-9 the community-utility argument and its answer.

title: From Seed to Plant
author: Gail Gibbons
rationale: The labeled-diagram nonfiction format is excellent for 5-6 science learners but underdense for 7-9 who need greater concept depth in plant biology; Gibbons designs this as a foundation text, not a primary resource for fluent readers with developing domain interests.

title: Gigi and Ojiji
author: Melissa Iwai
rationale: Early-reader chapter format doesn't support pre-reader engagement; the nonverbal-communication-across-language-barrier concept, while emotionally resonant at all ages, is delivered through a chapter structure that pre-readers cannot independently follow or meaningfully track as a read-aloud.

title: Hair Love
author: Matthew A. Cherry
rationale: The emotional depth of Mom's revealed absence (cancer treatment implied) elevates this beyond a hair-styling story for 7-9; the texture science, Black hair cultural knowledge, and fatherhood-as-practice theme give all three bands substantive content at different registers.

title: Henry, Like Always
author: Jenn Bailey
rationale: Early-reader chapter format disqualifies Wonderer; the predictable-sequence structure and routine-anxiety content are calibrated for the emerging reader's literacy development and cannot be delivered effectively as a pre-reader read-aloud.

title: Hot Dog
author: Doug Salati
rationale: Hot Dog is primarily a sensory and emotional experience book; the urban ecology and heat science are present but at visual picture-book surface density, leaving no second layer of conceptual substance for a fluent 7-9 reader who decodes the dog's-eye-view premise quickly.

title: How a House Is Built
author: Gail Gibbons
rationale: The complete technical construction sequence (surveying, foundation, framing, roofing, plumbing, electrical, finishing — each trade named and visualized) carries genuine engineering content across all three bands; 7-9 bring developing systematic thinking to the trade vocabulary and professional sequence.

title: How Dinosaurs Went Extinct: A Safety Guide
author: Ame Dyckman
rationale: Real paleontology and mass extinction science (Chicxulub asteroid impact, climate change, food chain collapse) embedded in absurdist safety-poster format gives 7-9 both the comedy structure to appreciate and the genuine science to extract; each band engages a different layer of the same double-coded content.

title: How to Count to 1
author: Casper Salmon
rationale: The cardinality and visual-counting concept is foundational mathematics already mastered by 7-9; the mathematical comedy (count one thing in a spread full of many) lands once but offers no expanding layer for a fluent reader with established number sense.

title: How to Hatch: A Gosling's Guide to Breaking Free
author: Sara Holly Ackerman
rationale: Pre-reader text density and single-topic biological focus (egg hatching mechanics: air cell, pip reflex, shell-breaking) present real science at a density too thin for 7-9 primary content; the entry-level biology does not expand into the depth 7-9 domain science learners need.

title: I Did It!
author: Michael Emberley
rationale: Early-reader chapter format disqualifies Wonderer; at 7-9 the simple-sentences/repetition structure and tiny-triumph self-efficacy concept read as calibrated for the 5-6 band — the gap between tiny accomplishment and enormous pride is developmentally a 5-6 insight, not a 7-9 one.

title: I Hear the Snow, I Smell the Sea
author: Janice Milusich
rationale: Early-reader reading level and the abstract sensory neuroscience concept (perceiving the environment differently) exceed Wonderer's concrete-operational requirement; Raschka's expressionist illustration style doesn't provide the sequential visual narrative pre-readers need to follow the story independently.

title: I Like Myself!
author: Karen Beaumont
rationale: The affirmation-rhyme format and body vocabulary content are calibrated for pre-readers and kindergartners; at 7-9 the concept density and register read as 'for little kids' without a second layer — a fluent reader processes the entire text in under 2 minutes.

title: Iggy Peck, Architect
author: Andrea Beaty
rationale: Real architecture and landmark references, engineering physics, and art history content give 7-9 substantive academic hooks; Beaty's sophisticated rhyming verse doesn't read as baby-register and the STEM content carries for domain-interested Artisans building on prior knowledge.

title: Invisible Things
author: Andy J. Pizza
rationale: The layered invisible-force framework (physics: gravity, magnetism, sound waves; biology: growth, digestion; philosophy: friendship and love) carries genuine concept density for all three bands; 7-9 engage the scientific vocabulary as real science alongside the philosophical dimension.

title: Ish
author: Peter Reynolds
rationale: The perfectionism-permission concept is relevant at 7-9 but delivered at picture-book density with no expanding second layer; a fluent reader grasps the 'ish' concept immediately and finds nothing new to extract from the brief text and simple narrative.

title: Lilly's Purple Plastic Purse
author: Kevin Henkes
rationale: The relational rupture arc (impulse → consequence → regret → repair → forgiveness), while emotionally accurate, is compressed into a K-1 mouse picture book that 7-9 readers decode immediately — no conceptual second layer requires this band's cognitive capacity.

title: Mama Miti: Wangari Maathai and the Trees of Kenya
author: Donna Jo Napoli
rationale: The layered biography/history/science/geography content (Wangari Maathai's Nobel-winning environmental activism, Kenyan geography, political history of the Green Belt Movement) carries genuine academic depth; 7-9 studying world history and environmental science engage this as primary content.

title: Maybe Something Beautiful
author: F. Isabel Campoy & Theresa Howell
rationale: The real-world civic art content (Barrio Logan Urban Art Trail, community organizing as civic infrastructure, color theory as collective action) gives 7-9 substantive content in art history and civics; Lopez's authentic mural illustrations add place-based and art history dimensions.

title: Mike Mulligan and His Steam Shovel
author: Virginia Lee Burton
rationale: The economic history content (technological obsolescence, labor displacement by diesel, civic infrastructure investment) and Burton's intricate architectural pen-and-ink illustrations carry genuine historical and engineering substance for 7-9 beyond the machine-story surface.

title: My Daddy Is a Cowboy
author: Stephanie Seales
rationale: Empty orbital_description field prevents proper band-fit evaluation; subjects field lists social-emotional only, which suggests the Artisan (7-9) band may be a forced fit, but Amy should confirm concept depth before demoting — specifically whether Black cowboy representation and fatherhood content carry a second layer for 7-9.

title: Nell Plants a Tree
author: Anne Wynter
rationale: The philosophy of planting what you won't see fully grown, multigenerational community history, and forest ecology through a complete tree life cycle carry genuine depth for 7-9; Miyares's time-passage illustrations (changing light and season across generations) are artistically sophisticated.

title: Officer Buckle and Gloria
author: Peggy Rathmann
rationale: The trust-collapse and partnership-repair content is genuine but packaged in a K-2 comedy picture book without concept density to engage 7-9; the safety-rule content is calibrated for younger children and a fluent reader fully processes the trust arc in a single sitting.

title: Once Upon a Book
author: Grace Lin
rationale: Literary self-reference and narrative meta-cognition require an existing reader's relationship to books that pre-literate 3-4 haven't yet formed; the recursive structure (girl enters her own book) lands only once a child already reads and understands books as objects with interiors.

title: Over and Under the Pond
author: Kate Messner
rationale: The above/below pond ecosystem split is an elegant structural concept but is presented at picture-book density insufficient for 7-9; the ecological detail (species listed above and below the water line) doesn't reach the depth a 7-9 science learner needs as primary content.

title: Owl and Penguin
author: Vikram Madan
rationale: Early-reader chapter format disqualifies Wonderer; the nocturnal/diurnal biological conflict is presented through a chapter structure that pre-readers cannot independently follow or sustain as a read-aloud.

title: Owl Moon
author: Jane Yolen
rationale: Yolen's elevated prose style is substantive for 7-9 who can appreciate poetic nature writing as a craft; the winter ecology science (owl species, nocturnal behavior, patient observation as scientific method) and the 'art of stillness' give 7-9 both literary and scientific content.

title: Popo the Xolo
author: Paloma Angelina Lopez
rationale: Aztec underworld mythology and pre-Columbian Mexico geography require prior cultural knowledge that exceeds 3-4's concrete-world frame; the early-reader reading level and mythology layer both push above Wonderer's pre-literacy and concrete-operational requirements.

title: Rosie Revere, Engineer
author: Andrea Beaty
rationale: The WWII historical context (Rosie the Riveter reference), engineering design cycle (failure as iteration data), and growth mindset philosophy give 7-9 substantive content; Beaty's sophisticated verse and the Great-Great-Aunt Rose biographical anchor carry literary depth beyond the invention comedy.

title: Roxaboxen
author: Alice McLerran
rationale: The childhood geography and social-play concepts, while meaningful, are presented at picture-book density; a 7-9 navigating complex real social structures finds the Roxaboxen model (pebbles and broken glass as social architecture) too simplified to engage as primary content.

title: Sam and Dave Dig a Hole
author: Mac Barnett
rationale: Genuine geological content (underground layers, diamond formation, what lies beneath) paired with Barnett's narratively sophisticated circular ending (the mystery children must solve to understand what happened) gives 7-9 both scientific and literary content; Klassen's illustrations carry visual puzzle depth.

title: Stellaluna
author: Janell Cannon
rationale: The bat biology content (echolocation, nocturnal behavior, fruit-eating adaptations) and the biology appendix specifically serve older readers; the identity theme (belonging vs. being yourself) is authentic 7-9 territory as peer pressure intensifies, giving this genuine dual-register substance.

title: Stop That Mop!
author: Jonathan Fenske
rationale: Early-reader format disqualifies Wonderer; at 7-9 the escalating-comedy cause-and-effect concept and early-reader density are calibrated for the 5-6 band (Geisel Award target: beginning readers), reading as conceptually thin for fluent 7-9 readers who have long internalized compounding-problem narrative structure.

title: Sulwe
author: Lupita Nyong'o
rationale: The astronomy content (star formation, light/shadow mechanics in the Day-Night fable), colorism as a social-cultural concept, and Kenyan visual culture through Harrison's illustrations give 7-9 substantive multi-domain content; the cosmological fable is sophisticated enough to carry at this band.

title: Swimmy
author: Leo Lionni
rationale: Swimmy's ocean ecosystem and schooling-as-defense concept are scientifically accurate but presented at pre-reader picture-book density; the cooperation lesson is familiar territory for 7-9 and the brief text offers no second layer requiring this band's cognitive capacity.

title: The Arguers
author: Corinna Luyken
rationale: Early-reader reading level and the meta-quality of argument-as-narrative-structure exceed Wonderer's concrete-operational ceiling; the fairy tale logic framing requires genre familiarity pre-readers haven't yet built, making the recursive joke inaccessible at the 3-4 band.

title: The Day the Crayons Quit
author: Drew Daywalt
rationale: The letter-format persuasive writing structure and color psychology content (each crayon's complaint encodes real color associations: red=overwork, white=invisibility, blue=scale) carry genuine instructional substance for 7-9 writing learners; the professional-communication meta-level lands specifically at this band.

title: The Dot
author: Peter H. Reynolds
rationale: The artistic confidence and color theory content are delivered at picture-book density; a 7-9 grasps the mentorship-and-permission theme immediately and the brief text offers no second conceptual layer to sustain engagement by a fluent reader.

title: The Keeping Quilt
author: Patricia Polacco
rationale: The multigenerational immigration history, textile arts as memory archive, and Polacco's real family biography give 7-9 substantive content across history, craft, and cultural transmission; each generation adding to the quilt's story models how objects carry history — a genuinely sophisticated concept for this band.

title: The Listening Walk
author: Paul Showers
rationale: The sound physics content is presented at neighborhood-observation level — onomatopoeia and listening attention — insufficient for 7-9; a fluent reader decodes the entire scientific content of the walk in under 4 minutes with no second layer requiring Artisan-level engagement.

title: The Little House
author: Virginia Lee Burton
rationale: A century of American urbanization (transportation history: horse-to-elevated-train-to-subway, environmental change, urban sprawl and renewal) compressed into a single picture book; Burton's intricate architectural illustrations function as historical documents that reward careful study at 7-9.

title: The Recess Queen
author: Alexis O'Neill
rationale: The bullying-intervention model (unafraid friendliness, invitation to play) is genuine social psychology but packaged at K-2 picture-book density; a 7-9's actual peer dynamics are more complex than the jump-rope-together solution, and the format reads as 'for little kids' without a second layer.

title: The Relatives Came
author: Cynthia Rylant
rationale: The sensory richness of family reunion and Virginia geography are presented at picture-book density without a second layer; the emotional content (summer warmth, ache of goodbye) is accessible but not conceptually engaging for 7-9 as primary content — it reads as nostalgic rather than substantive.

title: The Snail and the Whale
author: Julia Donaldson
rationale: World geography content (icebergs, volcanoes, beaches, coral reefs as named distinct ecosystems) and marine biology (whale stranding and rescue mechanics) give 7-9 substantive geographic and ecological content; Donaldson's sophisticated rhyme carries at this band without baby-register.

title: The Truth about Dragons
author: Julie Leung
rationale: Comparative mythology (Eastern vs. Western dragon traditions placed side by side) and the epistemological lesson ('truth changes depending on where you stand') are substantive philosophy and world history content; 7-9 engage the comparative analysis most fully as they begin cross-cultural study.

title: The Ugly Five
author: Julia Donaldson
rationale: The evolutionary adaptation concept (each ugly feature is a survival advantage) is genuine biology but presented at picture-book rhyme density; 7-9 with biology interest will have outpaced this level, and the African savanna geography is listed but not developed deeply enough to carry the band independently.

title: The Water Princess
author: Susan Verde
rationale: The memoir-backed water access story carries geography (Burkina Faso), water science (access, contamination, distance-to-source), and social justice content that engages 7-9 across multiple academic domains; the real basis (Georgie Badiel's childhood) gives it biographical and historical weight.

title: The Yellow Bus
author: Loren Long
rationale: The philosophy-of-purpose content and ecological transformation (bus-as-habitat) could carry genuine depth for 7-9 or read as thin contemplative picture book; 'contemplative ode' descriptions can mean either sparse-text-beautiful-images (demote 7-9) or genuinely philosophical text — Amy should confirm text density before classifying.

title: This Is Not My Hat
author: Jon Klassen
rationale: Klassen's visual-literary sophistication (the big fish's eyes narrate the true story before text confirms it) gives 7-9 genuine visual literacy content; the dark irony of the small fish's rationalizations and the ocean habitat add scientific and literary layers a fluent reader can analyze.

title: Thunder Cake
author: Patricia Polacco
rationale: The meteorology physics (counting seconds between lightning and thunder to calculate storm distance), food science (baking chemistry from scratch), and psychological reframing strategy (purposeful action transforms fear) give 7-9 substantive multi-domain content; Polacco's dense illustration style carries additional observational detail.

title: Tops and Bottoms
author: Janet Stevens
rationale: The plant science (which edible parts grow above vs. below ground) is foundational knowledge already familiar to 7-9; the Appalachian trickster tale structure is enjoyable but the concept density is calibrated for concrete-operational early-elementary learners rather than fluent Artisan readers.

title: Unflappable
author: Matthew Ward
rationale: The engineering design cycle (iterate-fail-learn, each failure informing the next machine) with diagram-specific machine drawings and flightless bird anatomy gives 7-9 substantive STEM content; the persistence psychology is developmentally well-timed as domain interests and performance stakes intensify.

title: We Are Water Protectors
author: Carole Lindstrom
rationale: The Indigenous environmental philosophy, Standing Rock historical context, and water science (water as interconnected ecological system) give 7-9 substantive content in environmental science, Indigenous history, and social justice; the Caldecott Medal illustration quality adds visual and cultural depth.

title: Wemberly Worried
author: Kevin Henkes
rationale: Wemberly's worry inventory is age-calibrated for preschool concerns (radiator, sandbox); at 7-9 anxiety is real but the K-1 picture-book delivery doesn't match the complexity of this band's social landscape, and the format reads as 'for little kids' without a second layer.

title: What Do You Do with a Chance
author: Kobi Yamada
rationale: The opportunity cost concept and philosophical framing are relevant at 7-9 but delivered at inspirational-picture-book density; the sparse text and social-emotional-only subject framing don't carry sufficient concept weight for 7-9 as primary content — the concept is grasped immediately without an expanding layer.
